facts.text: On this date in 1822, Brazil declared independence from Portugal — making it the only country in the Americas to have ever been the seat of a European monarchy, when the Portuguese royal family ruled from Rio de Janeiro.

On September 7, 1940, the Blitz began over London. The city absorbed 57 consecutive nights of bombing yet never surrendered its underground rail system, which sheltered up to 177,000 people per night.
More people live inside a 4,000km radius centered on Bangladesh than live outside it — over half of humanity fits within that single circle.
Monaco is so dense that if the entire world matched its population per square kilometer, every human alive today would fit inside Texas with room to spare for another two trillion people.
Canada has more lakes than every other country on Earth combined — roughly 60% of the world's lakes are Canadian, yet the country ranks 38th in population.
On this day in 1998, Google Inc. was incorporated in a Menlo Park garage with $100,000 in seed money. It is now worth more than the entire GDP of Italy.
On September 7, 1869, the first U.S. trademark was issued — to a paint company. The patent office now processes over 600,000 trademark applications a year.
The New York Stock Exchange was founded under a buttonwood tree in 1792. The original 24 brokers agreed to charge each other fixed commissions, an arrangement that lasted 183 years.
Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway originally made textiles. He later called buying it the worst trade of his life, estimating the opportunity cost at $200 billion.
The Dutch East India Company, history's first publicly traded corporation, was so large it had its own army, minted its own coins, and negotiated its own treaties with foreign governments.
On this day in 1927, Philo Farnsworth transmitted the first all-electronic television image — a straight line — to a receiver in the next room. He was 21.
On this day in 1936, the last known thylacine died in a Hobart zoo, making it the only large predator hunted to extinction in modern Australia.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere roughly 20 kilometers across, making its surface gravity 200 billion times stronger than Earth's.
Your body contains roughly 37 trillion cells, yet the decisions governing them are encoded in a molecule so thin that all the DNA in one human cell, uncoiled, would stretch about two meters.
Mantis shrimp see with 16 types of color receptors — humans have 3 — yet they process color worse than we do, trading nuance for raw speed in identifying threats.
On this day in 1936, the last known thylacine died in a Hobart zoo — not from hunting, but neglect. The species had survived 11 million years and was killed by a budget cut.
Oxford University was already 300 years old when the Aztec Empire was founded. Medieval Europe had tenure disputes before Tenochtitlán had walls.
On this day in 1822, Brazil declared independence from Portugal — while its emperor, Pedro I, was wearing riding boots and standing in a field. The paperwork caught up later.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She was ancient history to ancient Egyptians.
The fax machine was invented before the telephone. Alexander Bain patented a working fax system in 1843; Bell's telephone came 33 years later.

Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows, 2012 — and now it spreads like a word that always deserved to exist.
Vellichor (n.): the strange wistfulness of used bookshops. Also Koenig's invention — proof that naming a feeling retroactively makes you realize you've always had it.
On this day in 1888, the word 'appendicitis' appeared in print for the first time, coined by surgeon Reginald Fitz. Before that, the organ had no official name — and neither did dying from it.
Psithurism (n.): the sound of wind through leaves. From Greek psithuros, whispering. English had this word and quietly forgot it, which is its own kind of loss.
On September 7, 1822, Brazil declared independence — giving the world 'saudade,' Portuguese's untranslatable ache for something beloved and gone, a word the language exports better than any product.
On this date in 2017, China's PBOC banned ICOs entirely, declaring them illegal fundraising. Bitcoin dropped 10% within hours, then fully recovered in under two weeks.
On this date in 2021, El Salvador made Bitcoin legal tender — the first nation to do so. The rollout crashed the state-built Chivo wallet within hours of launch.
The Bitcoin genesis block contains the text 'The Times 03/Jan/2009 Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks' — hardcoded proof-of-timestamp that also reads as a political manifesto.
Ethereum's EIP-1559, live since August 2021, burns the base fee rather than paying it to miners. Over 4 million ETH had been destroyed by end of 2024, making ETH periodically deflationary.

The 2016 DAO hack didn't steal funds directly — it exploited a reentrancy bug to drain ETH before balances updated. The attacker had a 28-day timer built into the contract that gave Ethereum time to fork.

On this date in 2017, OpenAI released its Baselines library — clean RL reference implementations that quietly became the field's standard starting point for nearly every policy gradient experiment for years afterward.

On this date in 2022, the paper 'Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models' was posted to arXiv, naming a phenomenon researchers had noticed but not yet systematized: capabilities that appear sharply at scale rather than gradually.

AlphaFold2 predicted structures for over 200 million proteins — essentially the entire UniProt database — at a cost that would have taken wet-lab crystallography roughly 1,000 years of researcher time.

The original transformer in 'Attention Is All You Need' had 65 million parameters and was trained on 4.5 million sentence pairs. GPT-4 is estimated to be roughly 10,000 times larger by parameter count.
RLHF, the technique that made ChatGPT feel usable, was first applied to language models in a 2019 OpenAI paper on summarization — three years before most people encountered its effects.
